key_insight: PISA introduces a preconditioned, inexact stochastic ADMM optimizer for deep models that supports heterogeneous data and a wide range of preconditioners, offering provable convergence under weak assumptions and strong empirical gains over standard optimizers.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between theoretically-sound ADMM-style optimization and practical deep learning: handling data heterogeneity, allowing inexpensive (inexact) subproblem solves, and integrating flexible preconditioning without sacrificing convergence or scalability.
method: Formulates a preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM framework tailored for deep networks, where subproblems may be solved approximately to reduce cost.
Introduces flexible preconditioners (user-defined or adaptive) inside the ADMM updates to improve conditioning across heterogeneous data and model layers.
Provides theoretical convergence guarantees under minimal assumptions and validates empirical performance across diverse tasks versus standard baselines.
impact: Offers practitioners a scalable, robust optimizer that reduces tuning and computation while improving convergence and performance on heterogeneous datasets and distributed setups—useful for federated, multi-domain, and large-scale training.
visual_elements: Algorithm flowchart: ADMM update loop showing preconditioner and inexact subproblem solve steps
Comparison bar chart: validation accuracy or loss vs Adam/SGD/ADMM baselines across multiple tasks
Convergence plot: training loss vs iterations showing theoretical vs empirical behavior and effect of preconditioning
Schematic: heterogeneous-data setup (multiple clients/domains) with centralized variable fusion to illustrate applicability
paper_title: Preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM for deep models
paper_authors: Shenglong Zhou, Ouya Wang, Ziyan Luo, Yongxu Zhu, Geoffrey Ye Li
